title: Baghrir (Moroccan thousand-hole semolina pancakes)
steps: Blend the semolina, flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, salt and the warm water for 2 minutes until the batter is smooth and bubbly.
Cover the batter and leave for 30 to 40 minutes until foamy.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Do not grease it.
Pour in a ladleful of batter and spread it a little. Bubbles will rise and burst to leave tiny holes.
Cook on one side only for about 2 minutes, until the top is dry and no wet batter remains. Do not flip.
Stack the pancakes between a clean cloth to keep them soft. Serve with warm honey and butter.

title: Bissara (Moroccan fava bean soup)

ingredients.name: dried peeled split fava beans (or split peas), soaked overnight
lemon wedges and fresh bread, to serve

steps: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a pot with the garlic and water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for 45 to 60 minutes until the beans are completely soft.
Blend the soup with a stick blender until very smooth, adding a little hot water if it is too thick.
Stir in half the olive oil, the cumin and salt and heat through.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the rest of the oil, dust with paprika and extra cumin and serve with lemon wedges and bread.

title: Briouat (Moroccan crisp pastry parcels with spiced beef and cheese)

ingredients.name: feta or soft goat cheese, crumbled

steps: Fry the onion in the oil until soft, add the beef and spices and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until browned and dry.
Cool the mixture, then fold in the herbs, cheese, salt and pepper.
Cut each pastry sheet into 3 long strips and keep them covered with a damp cloth so they do not dry out.
Brush a strip with butter, put a spoonful of filling near one end and fold the corner over to make a triangle. Keep folding along the strip into a neat triangular parcel, sealing the end with butter.
Bake at 200 C for 12 to 15 minutes until golden, or fry in shallow oil for 2 minutes per side.
Serve hot as a starter with lemon wedges.

title: Chebakia (Moroccan sesame and honey flower cookies)
steps: Mix the flour, half the sesame seeds, spices and baking powder. Rub in the butter.
Add the egg, vinegar, 1 tablespoon of orange blossom water and enough water to make a smooth, pliable dough. Knead for 5 minutes and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into rectangles of about 6 by 10 cm. Make 4 parallel slits in each rectangle, then thread the corners through the slits to form a rose shape.
Heat the oil to about 170 C and fry the cookies in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden.
Warm the honey with the water and the remaining orange blossom water in a wide pan. Dip each hot cookie into the honey for 30 seconds.
Drain, scatter with the rest of the sesame seeds and leave to dry. Store airtight.

title: Chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives (Moroccan chicken stew)
steps: Mix the chicken with the garlic, ginger, turmeric, saffron, salt and pepper and leave for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a tagine base or heavy pot and cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and brown lightly, then pour in the water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently for 40 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Scatter with the herbs and serve with couscous or bread.

title: Fish tagine with chermoula (Moroccan fish and vegetable stew)

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillets (hake, cod or monkfish), in large pieces

steps: Blend the garlic, coriander, parsley, cumin, paprika, lemon juice, 3 tablespoons of the oil, chilli and salt into a chermoula marinade.
Coat the fish with half the chermoula and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Spread the remaining oil in a wide pot or tagine. Layer the carrots and potatoes first, then season with salt and add 100 ml of water.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
Lay the fish on top, add the tomatoes and pepper, spoon over the rest of the chermoula, cover and cook for 15 to 20 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Serve from the pot with bread.

title: Gazelle ankles (Moroccan almond-paste crescent cookies)
steps: Mix the flour, salt, melted butter and orange blossom water, then add cold water gradually to make a soft, smooth dough. Rest for 20 minutes.
For the filling, combine the ground almonds, icing sugar, cinnamon, orange blossom water, soft butter and egg white into a paste. Roll it into small logs or crescents.
Heat the oven to 170 C.
Roll the dough out very thin and cut into strips. Place an almond log on a strip and wrap the dough around it, trimming and sealing the edges. Curve into a crescent.
Prick lightly with a needle so the cookies do not burst, place on a tray and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until just pale golden.
Cool and dust with icing sugar if you like. Serve with mint tea.

title: Harira (Moroccan tomato, lentil and chickpea soup)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef, cut into small cubes
each fresh coriander and parsley, chopped
plain flour mixed with 100 ml water

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the meat with the onion, celery, ginger, turmeric, pepper and cinnamon for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, saffron, lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 40 minutes until the lentils and meat are tender.
Add the chickpeas, herbs and salt and simmer for another 10 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour and water mixture, then stir it slowly into the soup and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes more, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and dates to break the fast, as is traditional during Ramadan.

title: Matbucha (Moroccan slow-cooked tomato and pepper relish)

ingredients.name: red bell peppers, roasted, peeled and chopped

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the garlic and chilli. Stir for 30 seconds without browning.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, sugar and salt and bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, as the juices reduce.
Add the chopped roasted peppers and continue cooking for 30 to 40 minutes until the mixture is dark, thick and jammy, stirring more often near the end.
Taste for salt. Serve warm or cold with bread, or use as a sauce for eggs or fish.

title: Mechoui (Moroccan slow-roasted spiced lamb shoulder)
steps: Mash the butter with the garlic, cumin, paprika, pepper and salt into a paste.
Rub the paste all over the lamb, working it into the cuts you make across the meat. Leave for 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 160 C. Place the lamb in a roasting tin on a rack with the water in the base and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 3 to 3.5 hours, basting with the juices every hour, until the meat is so tender it pulls away from the bone.
Remove the foil, increase the heat to 220 C and roast for 15 minutes to brown the surface.
Rest for 15 minutes and serve by pulling the meat off with your fingers, with cumin and salt on the side for dipping.

title: Mrouzia (Moroccan lamb tagine with raisins, almonds and honey)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or neck, in large pieces

steps: Place the lamb, onions, ras el hanout, ginger, saffron, cinnamon stick, butter and salt in a heavy pot or tagine and mix to coat.
Add the water, cover and cook over low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours, turning the meat now and then, until it is very tender.
Soak the raisins in hot water for 15 minutes and drain.
Lift out the lamb, then add the raisins and honey to the sauce and simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes until thick and syrupy.
Return the lamb to the pot, coat in the sauce and heat through.
Serve topped with the toasted almonds, with bread for dipping.

title: Msemmen (Moroccan layered square flatbread)

ingredients.name: fine semolina, plus extra for dusting
butter, melted, mixed with 4 tbsp oil

steps: Mix the flour, semolina, salt and sugar, add the water and knead for 10 minutes into a very smooth, elastic dough. Divide into 10 balls, coat with oil and rest for 15 minutes.
On an oiled surface, stretch one ball with your fingers into a very thin square, brushing with the butter-oil mixture and dusting with a little semolina.
Fold the sides into the centre like an envelope to make a small square, then repeat with the others, resting them for 10 minutes.
Flatten each square gently with your fingertips or a rolling pin into a thin square about 15 cm wide.
Cook on a hot, dry griddle or frying pan for about 2 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Serve warm with honey, butter, jam or soft cheese, or with mint tea.

title: Pastilla (Moroccan chicken and almond pie with cinnamon sugar)

ingredients.name: each fresh parsley and coriander, chopped
icing sugar, plus extra for dusting

steps: In a pot, cook the chicken with the onions, ginger, turmeric, saffron, cinnamon stick, oil, salt, pepper and 300 ml of water. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the meat is falling off the bone.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones. Remove the cinnamon stick.
Reduce the cooking liquid until about 150 ml remains, lower the heat, beat in the eggs and stir gently until they form soft curds. Fold in the herbs and let cool.
Mix the toasted almonds with 2 tablespoons of icing sugar and the ground cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 190 C. Brush a 24 cm round tin with butter and overlap 4 pastry sheets so they hang over the edge, brushing each with butter.
Fill with half the egg mixture, then the shredded chicken, the almond mixture and the rest of the eggs. Fold the pastry overhang over the top and cover with 2 more sheets, tucking the edges under.
Brush with butter and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Dust with icing sugar and cinnamon lines and serve warm.

title: Rfissa (Moroccan chicken with lentils, fenugreek and shredded flatbread)

ingredients.name: msemmen or paratha flatbreads, torn into small pieces

steps: Soak the fenugreek seeds in water for 30 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pot, add the onions, spices, fenugreek and chicken and brown the chicken lightly for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 45 to 50 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is reduced and thick with lentils.
Meanwhile, tear the flatbreads into thin strips and warm them in a dry pan or in a low oven, then place them on a large platter.
Steam or moisten the bread with a few ladlefuls of the cooking liquid.
Arrange the chicken on the bread and spoon the lentils and sauce over everything. Serve at once, traditionally shared from the platter.

title: Sellou (Moroccan toasted flour, almond and sesame sweet)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Spread the flour on a tray and toast for about 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until light golden and nutty. Let it cool.
Toast the almonds for 8 to 10 minutes until golden, then cool and grind them coarsely.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Sift the cooled flour into a large bowl and mix in the almonds, sesame seeds, aniseed, cinnamon and icing sugar.
Warm the butter with the honey, pour into the mixture and rub with your hands until it clumps when pressed.
Pile into a mound or press into a dish, decorate with extra almonds and serve in small spoonfuls with tea.

title: Taktouka (Moroccan roasted pepper and tomato salad)
steps: Roast the peppers under a hot grill or over a flame, turning until blistered all over. Cover and let them steam for 10 minutes.
Peel off the skins, remove the seeds and chop the flesh finely.
Peel the tomatoes by dropping them in boiling water for 1 minute, then chop them.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes, paprika, cumin, chilli and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, add the peppers and cook for another 15 minutes until thick and most liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the parsley and serve at room temperature as a dip or side.

title: Tangia (Marrakesh slow-baked beef with preserved lemon and cumin)

ingredients.name: beef shin or shank, in large chunks

steps: Heat the oven to 150 C.
Mix the beef with the garlic, cumin, paprika, saffron, smen or butter, olive oil, salt and pepper in a deep ovenproof pot or a clay pot.
Tuck the preserved lemon pieces between the meat and add the water.
Cover with a double layer of baking parchment tied or pressed down, then put on the lid so the pot is tightly sealed.
Bake for 4 to 5 hours without opening, until the meat is falling apart and bathed in a rich, buttery sauce.
Serve straight from the pot with fresh bread.

title: Vegetable tagine with chickpeas (Moroccan spiced vegetable stew)

ingredients.name: pumpkin or butternut squash, in chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the carrots, potatoes and pumpkin with the tomatoes, 200 ml of water and salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, then add the courgette, chickpeas and dried fruit.
Cook for another 15 to 20 minutes, partly covered, until all the vegetables are tender and the sauce is thick.
Top with coriander and serve with couscous or bread.

title: Zaalouk (Moroccan smoky aubergine and tomato salad)
steps: Pierce the aubergines and roast them whole at 220 C or char them over a flame for 30 to 40 minutes until collapsed and soft.
Cool slightly, then peel and chop the flesh coarsely.
Heat the oil in a pan, add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Cook the tomatoes for 10 minutes until thick, then add the aubergine and mash it into the sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until it has the texture of a thick, chunky dip. Stir in the coriander and lemon juice.
Serve warm or cold with crusty bread.
